```{r}

# Setting the Path

library(readr)

datapath <- "C:/Users/ellave3/OneDrive - Georgia Institute of Technology/Documents/GitHub/OLNOLTimecourses/RSA_graphs/sourceData"

filenames <- list.files(
  path = datapath,
  pattern = "^matlab_rsa_spreadsheet_RAW.*\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

stopifnot(length(filenames) > 0)

newest_file <- filenames[which.max(file.info(filenames)$mtime)]

data.raw <- read_csv(newest_file, show_col_types = FALSE) #grabs the most up to date spreadsheet

```

```{r}
# DATA CLEANING AND RELABELING

# 1) pivoting > long format

long_raw <- data.raw %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -ID,
    names_to = "raw_name",
    values_to = "RSA"
  )

# 2) Parse variables

long_parsed <- long_raw %>%
  mutate(
    ROI = case_when(
      str_detect(raw_name, "hippo") ~ "Hippocampus",
      str_detect(raw_name, "RSComplex") ~ "Complex",
      str_detect(raw_name, "ba2930") ~ "RSC"
    ),
    
    learningStage = case_when(
      str_detect(raw_name, "_early_") ~ "Early",
      str_detect(raw_name, "_late_") ~ "Late"
    ),
  
    Hall = case_when(
      str_detect(raw_name, "_0") ~ "Cue period",
      str_detect(raw_name, "_1") ~ "1st hallway",
      str_detect(raw_name, "_2") ~ "2nd hallway",
      str_detect(raw_name, "_3") ~ "Goal"
   ),
  
Overlappicity = case_when(
  str_detect(raw_name, "^'?nol_") ~ "NOL",
  str_detect(raw_name, "^'?ol_")  ~ "OL"
  ),
  
  
  )



```

1) “how much does the representation of the environments change within a given ROI with learning [early & late]?” 
***********************************
**************************
HIPPOCAMPUS OL
**************************
# ---------> I have checked bonferroni and anovas values match JASP
-> Repeated measures ANOVA Learning stage (Early,Late) x Hall (Cue period, 1st hall, 2nd hall, goal)
(1) OL HC
```{r}

# 1) Filtering + Subject means
plot_data <- long_parsed %>%
  filter(
    ROI %in% c("Hippocampus"),     # ROI filter
    str_detect(raw_name, "ol_new_early_w_ol_new_early_|ol_new_late_w_ol_new_late_") 
  ) %>%
  group_by(ID, learningStage, Hall) %>%
  # summarise(RSA = mean(RSA, na.rm = TRUE),
  #           .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # Ensure Hall is a factor in the correct order
  mutate(Hall = factor(Hall,
                       levels = c("Cue period",
                                  "1st hallway",
                                  "2nd hallway",
                                  "Goal")))

print(plot_data)

```
ANOVA
```{r}

# summary
# I'll have to relabel 'anova_model', 'anova_table', etc if I don't want these data to be overwritten
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly")) #same analysis as in JASP
anova_model <- aov_ez(
  id = "ID",
  dv = "RSA",
  data = plot_data,
  within = c("learningStage", "Hall"),
  type = 3, # Type III SS (JASP style)
  anova_table = list(
    correction = "GG", # <-- Greenhouse–Geisser correction for when factors ≥3 levels (e.g., Halls)
    es = "pes"   # partial eta squared
  )
)

# # ANOVA TABLE
anova_table <- anova_model$anova_table
print(anova_table)

# Extract ANOVA table as data frame
anova_table <- as.data.frame(anova_model$anova_table)


# # Move row names (effects) into a column safely
 anova_table <- tibble::rownames_to_column(anova_table, var = "Effect")
 
# Format p-values like JASP
 format_p <- function(p) {
   if (p < .001) {
     "< .001"
  } else {
     paste0("= ", format(round(p, 3), nsmall = 3))
   }
 }

# # Clean ANOVA table
 niceAnovaTable <- data.frame(
   Effect = anova_table$Effect,
  df1    = anova_table[[1]],   # first column = numerator df
  df2    = anova_table[[2]],   # second column = denominator df
  F      = round(anova_table$F, 3),
  p      = sapply(anova_table$`Pr(>F)`, format_p),
  `η²p`   = round(anova_table$pes, 3) # partial eta-squared
)

print(niceAnovaTable)


```
POST-HOCs 
```{r}
library(emmeans)

# Estimated marginal means for ALL 8 cells
emm_interaction <- emmeans(anova_model, ~ learningStage * Hall)


# Holm correction
posthoc_holm <- pairs(emm_interaction, adjust = "holm")

holm_table <- summary(posthoc_holm) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    estimate = round(estimate, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    cohen_d = round(estimate / (SE * sqrt(2)), 3),  #
    t = round(t.ratio, 2),
    pHolms = ifelse(p.value < .001,
               "< 0.001",
               paste0("= ", round(p.value, 3)))
  )

holm_table

# Bonferroni correction
posthoc_bonf <- pairs(emm_interaction, adjust = "bonferroni")

bonferroni_table <- summary(posthoc_bonf) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    estimate = round(estimate, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    cohen_d = round(estimate / (SE * sqrt(2)), 3),  
    t = round(t.ratio, 2),
    pBonf = ifelse(p.value < .001,
               "< 0.001",
               paste0("= ", round(p.value, 3)))
  )

bonferroni_table
```
DESCRIPTIVES

```{r}
###) Descriptives
descriptives_OL_HC <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(learningStage, Hall) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = mean(RSA, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(RSA, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE = SD / sqrt(N),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Mean, SD, SE), ~ round(.x, 3)))

print(descriptives_OL_HC)
```
PLOTTING OL HIPPOCAMPUS (LearningStage x Hall)

```{r}

# 2) Plot with ribbon for mean ± SE
ggplot(plot_data,
       aes(x = Hall,
           y = RSA,
           color = learningStage,
           fill = learningStage,
           group = learningStage)) +
  
  # Ribbon for standard error
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se,
               geom = "ribbon",
               alpha = 0.15,
               color = NA) +
  
   # Mean line with Early dashed, Late solid
  stat_summary(fun = mean,
               geom = "line",
               aes(linetype = learningStage),
               linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Mean solid line
  # stat_summary(fun = mean,
  #              geom = "line",
  #              linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Mean points
  stat_summary(fun = mean,
               geom = "point",
               size = 3) +
  
  # Custom colors
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Early" = HC_OL_Early_orange,
    "Late" = HC_OL_Late_orange
  )) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
   "Early" = HC_OL_Early_orange,
    "Late" = HC_OL_Late_orange
  )) +
  
  # Line types
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(
    "Early" = "dashed",
    "Late" = "solid"
  )) +
  
  # Labels
  labs(x = "Hall",
       y = "Representational similarity (r)",
       title = "(2a) OL Learning Stage HC",
       # subtitle = "(2a) xxx",
       color = "Learning stage",
       fill = "Learning stage",
       linetype = "Learning stage") +
  
  # Clean theme
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

```

RSC NOL
**************************

-> Repeated meausures ANOVA Learning stage (Early,Late) x Hall (Cue period, 1st hall, 2nd hall, goal)
(1) NOL RSC 
```{r}

# 1) Filtering + Subject means
plot_data <- long_parsed %>%
  filter(
    ROI %in% c("RSC"),     # ROI filter
    str_detect(raw_name, "nol_new_early_w_nol_new_early_|nol_new_late_w_nol_new_late_") 
  ) %>%
  group_by(ID, learningStage, Hall) %>%
  
  # Ensure Hall is a factor in the correct order
  mutate(Hall = factor(Hall,
                       levels = c("Cue period",
                                  "1st hallway",
                                  "2nd hallway",
                                  "Goal")))

print(plot_data)

```
ANOVA
```{r}

# summary
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly")) #same analysis as in JASP
anova_model <- aov_ez(
  id = "ID",
  dv = "RSA",
  data = plot_data,
  within = c("learningStage", "Hall"),
  type = 3, # Type III SS (JASP style)
  anova_table = list(
    correction = "GG", # <-- Greenhouse–Geisser correction for when factors ≥3 levels (e.g., Halls)
    es = "pes"   # partial eta squared
  )
)

# # ANOVA TABLE
anova_table <- anova_model$anova_table
print(anova_table)

# Extract ANOVA table as data frame
anova_table <- as.data.frame(anova_model$anova_table)


# # Move row names (effects) into a column safely
 anova_table <- tibble::rownames_to_column(anova_table, var = "Effect")
 
# Format p-values like JASP
 format_p <- function(p) {
   if (p < .001) {
     "< .001"
  } else {
     paste0("= ", format(round(p, 3), nsmall = 3))
   }
 }

# # Clean ANOVA table
 niceAnovaTable <- data.frame(
   Effect = anova_table$Effect,
  df1    = anova_table[[1]],   # first column = numerator df
  df2    = anova_table[[2]],   # second column = denominator df
  F      = round(anova_table$F, 3),
  p      = sapply(anova_table$`Pr(>F)`, format_p),
  `η²p`   = round(anova_table$pes, 3) # partial eta-squared
)

print(niceAnovaTable)


```
POST-HOCs 
```{r}
library(emmeans)

# Estimated marginal means for ALL 8 cells
emm_interaction <- emmeans(anova_model, ~ learningStage * Hall)


# Holm correction
posthoc_holm <- pairs(emm_interaction, adjust = "holm")

holm_table <- summary(posthoc_holm) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    estimate = round(estimate, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    cohen_d = round(estimate / (SE * sqrt(2)), 3),  #
    t = round(t.ratio, 2),
    pHolms = ifelse(p.value < .001,
               "< 0.001",
               paste0("= ", round(p.value, 3)))
  )

holm_table

# Bonferroni correction
posthoc_bonf <- pairs(emm_interaction, adjust = "bonferroni")

bonferroni_table <- summary(posthoc_bonf) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    estimate = round(estimate, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    cohen_d = round(estimate / (SE * sqrt(2)), 3),  
    t = round(t.ratio, 2),
    pBonf = ifelse(p.value < .001,
               "< 0.001",
               paste0("= ", round(p.value, 3)))
  )

bonferroni_table
```
DESCRIPTIVES

```{r}
###) Descriptives
descriptives_NOL_RSC <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(learningStage, Hall) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = mean(RSA, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(RSA, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE = SD / sqrt(N),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Mean, SD, SE), ~ round(.x, 3)))

print(descriptives_NOL_RSC)
```
PLOTTING NOL RSC (LearningStage x Hall)

```{r}

# 2) Plot with ribbon for mean ± SE
ggplot(plot_data,
       aes(x = Hall,
           y = RSA,
           color = learningStage,
           fill = learningStage,
           group = learningStage)) +
  
  # Ribbon for standard error
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se,
               geom = "ribbon",
               alpha = 0.15,
               color = NA) +
  
# Mean line with Early dashed, Late solid
  stat_summary(fun = mean,
               geom = "line",
               aes(linetype = learningStage),
               linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Mean points
  stat_summary(fun = mean,
               geom = "point",
               size = 3) +
  
  # Custom colors
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Early" = RSC_NOL_Early_purple,
    "Late" = RSC_NOL_Late_purple
  )) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
   "Early" = RSC_NOL_Early_purple,
    "Late" = RSC_NOL_Late_purple
  )) +
  
  # Line types
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(
    "Early" = "dashed",
    "Late" = "solid"
  )) +
  
   # Labels
  labs(x = "Hall",
       y = "Representational similarity (r)",
       title = "(2a) OL Learning Stage RSC",
       color = "Learning stage",
       fill = "Learning stage",
       linetype = "Learning stage") +
  
  
  # Clean theme
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

```

```{r}

## Additional filters to add the RSComplex

# 1) Removing ROI filter -> we get all 3 ROIs 
plot_HC_RSC_Complex_Late_OL <- long_parsed %>%
  filter(
    str_detect(raw_name, "ol_new_late_w_ol_new_late_")  
  ) %>%
 

# Normalize RSComplex names so colors/legend map correctly
  mutate(
    ROI = dplyr::recode(ROI,
                        "Complex" = "RSComplex",
                        "RS Complex" = "RSComplex",
                        .default = ROI),
    
    # Lock ROI order to ensure consistent plotting/legend
    ROI = factor(ROI, levels = c("Hippocampus", "RSC", "RSComplex")),
    # Ensure Hall is ordered for the x-axis
    Hall = factor(Hall,
                  levels = c("Cue period",
                             "1st hallway",
                             "2nd hallway",
                             "Goal"))
  )

## Plotting the 3 ROIs
# 2) Plot with ribbon for mean ± SE
ggplot(plot_HC_RSC_Complex_Late_OL,
       aes(x = Hall,
           y = RSA,
           color = ROI,
           fill = ROI,
           group = ROI)) +
  
  # Ribbon for standard error
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se,
               geom = "ribbon",
               alpha = 0.15,
               color = NA) +
  
  # Mean line
  stat_summary(fun = mean,
               geom = "line",
               linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Mean points
  stat_summary(fun = mean,
               geom = "point",
               size = 3) +
  
  # Custom colors
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "RSC" = RSC_OL_Late_purple,
    "Hippocampus" = HC_OL_Late_orange,
    "RSComplex" = Complex_OL_Late_blue
  )) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "RSC" = RSC_OL_Late_purple,
    "Hippocampus" = HC_OL_Late_orange,
    "RSComplex" = Complex_OL_Late_blue
  )) +
  
  # Labels
  labs(x = "Hall",
       y = "Representational similarity (r)",
       title = "(2a) OL LATE HC vs RSC vs RSComplex",
       #subtitle = "(2a) OL EARLY HCvsRSC",
       color = "ROI",
       fill = "ROI") +
  
  # Clean theme
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)
```

```{r}
# (2a) NOL LATE HC vs Complex 

# 1) Filtering + Subject means
plot_data <- long_parsed %>%
  filter(
    ROI %in% c("Complex", "Hippocampus"),     # ROI filter
    str_detect(raw_name, "nol_new_late_w_nol_new_late_")  
  ) %>%
  group_by(ID, ROI, Hall) %>%
  # summarise(RSA = mean(RSA, na.rm = TRUE),
  #           .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # Ensure Hall is a factor in the correct order
  mutate(Hall = factor(Hall,
                       levels = c("Cue period",
                                  "1st hallway",
                                  "2nd hallway",
                                  "Goal")))

print(plot_data)

```
ANOVA
```{r}

 # ANOVA
# summary
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly")) #same analysis as in JASP
anova_model <- aov_ez(
  id = "ID",
  dv = "RSA",
  data = plot_data,
  within = c("ROI", "Hall"),
  type = 3, # Type III SS (JASP style)
  anova_table = list(
    es = "pes"   # partial eta squared
  )
)

# ANOVA TABLE
# anova_table <- anova_model$anova_table
# print(anova_table)
# Extract ANOVA table as data frame
anova_table <- as.data.frame(anova_model$anova_table)


# Move row names (effects) into a column safely
anova_table <- tibble::rownames_to_column(anova_table, var = "Effect")

# Format p-values like JASP
format_p <- function(p) {
  if (p < .001) {
    "< .001"
  } else {
    paste0("= ", format(round(p, 3), nsmall = 3))
  }
}

# Clean ANOVA table
niceAnovaTable <- data.frame(
  Effect = anova_table$Effect,
  df1    = anova_table[[1]],   # first column = numerator df
  df2    = anova_table[[2]],   # second column = denominator df
  F      = round(anova_table$F, 3),
  p      = sapply(anova_table$`Pr(>F)`, format_p),
  `η²p`   = round(anova_table$pes, 3) # partial eta-squared
)

print(niceAnovaTable)


```
DESCRIPTIVES
```{r}
###) Descriptives
descriptives_NOL_Late_HCvsComplex <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(ROI, Hall) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = mean(RSA, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(RSA, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE = SD / sqrt(N),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Mean, SD, SE), ~ round(.x, 3)))

print(descriptives_NOL_Late_HCvsComplex)
```

****************************
2) NATURE OF REPRESENTATIONS
****************************
REPULSION, SEPARATION OR COMPLETION REPRESENTATIONS?
******************************************************
## (2b) 2b.1) Hippocampus (EARLY+LATE)
```{r}

# 1) Set hall order
long_parsed <- long_parsed %>%
  mutate(Hall = factor(Hall,
                       levels = c("Cue period",
                                  "1st hallway",
                                  "2nd hallway",
                                  "Goal")))
# 2) Filter data

## Early
early_data <- long_parsed %>%
  filter(
    Overlappicity == "OL",
    learningStage == "Early",
    ROI %in% c("Hippocampus"),
    grepl("ol_new_early_w_ol_new_early|ol_new_early_w_ol_old_early", raw_name)
  )

## Late
late_data <- long_parsed %>%
  filter(
    Overlappicity == "OL",
    learningStage == "Late",
    ROI %in% c("Hippocampus"),
    grepl("ol_new_late_w_ol_new_late|ol_new_late_w_ol_old_late", raw_name)
  )


# 2) Reshape to wide format
## Early
early_wide <- early_data %>%
```

paired t-tests (for both Early & Late), Cohen's d, CI's 95%...
```{r}
library(dplyr)

run_full_paired_tests <- function(data, LearningStage_label) {

  data %>%
    group_by(Hall) %>%
    summarise(
      n = sum(!is.na(new_new) & !is.na(new_old)),
      
      mean_new_new = mean(new_new, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_new_old = mean(new_old, na.rm = TRUE),
      
      mean_diff = mean(new_new - new_old, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_diff   = sd(new_new - new_old, na.rm = TRUE),
      
      t_test = list(t.test(new_new, new_old, paired = TRUE)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    
    mutate(
      t_value = sapply(t_test, function(x) unname(x$statistic)),
      df      = sapply(t_test, function(x) unname(x$parameter)),
      p_value = sapply(t_test, function(x) x$p.value),
      
      ci_low  = sapply(t_test, function(x) x$conf.int[1]),
      ci_high = sapply(t_test, function(x) x$conf.int[2]),
      
      # Cohen's dz for paired samples
      cohens_d = mean_diff / sd_diff,
      
       # Standard error of the difference (SE)
      se_diff = sd_diff / sqrt(n), 
      
      # Flag significant p values
      se_diff = sd_diff / sqrt(n),
      sig_value = case_when(
        p_value < 0.001 ~ "***",
        p_value < 0.01  ~ "**",
        p_value < 0.05  ~ "*",
        TRUE            ~ ""
      ),
    
      
      leStage = LearningStage_label
    ) %>%
    
    select(
      leStage, Hall, n,
      mean_new_new, mean_new_old,
      mean_diff, sd_diff,se_diff,
      t_value, df, p_value,
      ci_low, ci_high,
      cohens_d, sig_value
    )
}

```
Data table
```{r}
early_results <- run_full_paired_tests(early_wide, "Early")
late_results  <- run_full_paired_tests(late_wide,  "Late")

final_results_HC <- bind_rows(early_results, late_results)
```

***************
# 3) CORRELATIONS
***************
# a) OVERLAPPING MAZES FIRST

### HIPPOCAMPUS + RSC

 HC + RSC OL EARLY
```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# --------------------------------
# 1) Filter + clean strings
# --------------------------------
heatmapFilter <- long_parsed %>%
  filter(
    ROI %in% c("RSC", "Hippocampus"),
    str_detect(raw_name, "ol_new_early_w_ol_new_early_")
  ) %>%
  group_by(ID, ROI, Hall) %>%
  mutate(
    # normalize the Hall names to avoid hidden mismatches
    Hall = str_squish(Hall),
    Hall = factor(Hall, levels = c("Cue period", "1st hallway", "2nd hallway", "Goal")),
    ROI  = str_squish(ROI)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Create combined condition label (normalized)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmapFilter <- heatmapFilter %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = str_squish(paste(ROI, Hall))
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Pivot to wide format
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_wide <- heatmapFilter %>%
  select(ID, Condition, RSA) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Condition,
    values_from = RSA
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Desired axis order (make sure it matches exactly)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
axis_order <- c(
  "Hippocampus Cue period",
  "Hippocampus 1st hallway",
  "Hippocampus 2nd hallway",
  "Hippocampus Goal",
  "RSC Cue period",
  "RSC 1st hallway",
  "RSC 2nd hallway",
  "RSC Goal"
)

# Sanity check
# print(setdiff(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide)))
# print(setdiff(colnames(heatmap_wide), axis_order))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute correlation matrix (restricted + reordered)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Keep only the columns in axis_order (in that order), dropping any others
present <- intersect(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide))
if (length(present) != length(axis_order)) {
  warning("Some expected conditions are missing: ",
          paste(setdiff(axis_order, present), collapse = ", "))
}
corr_matrix <- heatmap_wide %>%
  select(all_of(present)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Reorder rows/cols to the desired axis_order (for present labels)
corr_matrix <- corr_matrix[present, present, drop = FALSE]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute pairwise counts (n) and p-values for the matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------
data_wide <- heatmap_wide %>% select(all_of(present))
X <- as.matrix(data_wide)

# Pairwise non-NA counts: n_ij = number of rows where both cols i and j are not NA
ind   <- !is.na(X)
n_mat <- t(ind) %*% ind    # matrix of pairwise sample sizes

# We already have r_mat = corr_matrix (reordered to [present, present])
r_mat <- corr_matrix

# Compute p-values from r and n (two-sided); handle r = ±1, n < 3 safely
p_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(r_mat), ncol = ncol(r_mat),
                dimnames = dimnames(r_mat))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(r_mat))) {
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(r_mat))) {
    r <- r_mat[i, j]
    n <- n_mat[i, j]
    if (!is.na(r) && !is.na(n) && n >= 3) {
      if (abs(r) < 1) {
        tval <- r * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - r^2))
        pval <- 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = n - 2)
      } else {
        # Perfect correlation with >= 3 points -> p ~ 0
        pval <- 0
      }
      p_mat[i, j] <- pval
    } else {
      p_mat[i, j] <- NA_real_
    }
  }
}


# Choose which p-values to use for stars:
p_use <- p_mat  # or use p_adj_mat if you enabled BH correction above

# Build significance stars
stars_mat <- matrix("", nrow = nrow(p_use), ncol = ncol(p_use),
                    dimnames = dimnames(p_use))
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use < 0.001] <- "***"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.001 & p_use < 0.01] <- "**"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.01 & p_use < 0.05] <- "*"

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6)Convert correlation matrix (r mat) to long format and add p-values + stars
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(r_mat)) %>%
  rename(
    X_label = Var1,
    Y_label = Var2,
    cor     = Freq
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # attach p and stars from matrices (matching by dimnames)
    p_value = as.vector(p_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(p_mat)),
                                    match(Y_label, colnames(p_mat)))]),
    stars   = stars_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(stars_mat)),
                              match(Y_label, colnames(stars_mat)))],
    # format r with 3 decimals and append stars
    label_r = sprintf("%.3f", cor),
    label   = ifelse(is.na(cor), "", paste0(label_r, stars))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    X_label = factor(X_label, levels = present),
    Y_label = factor(Y_label, levels = present)
  )

# Freeze master copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df
# Freeze a clean copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df


```
## MASKING TRIANGLES
```{r}
## MASKING (UPPER OR LOWER) TRIANGLES

# Choose masking type
mask_type <- "none"   # "none", "upper", "lower", "upper_diag", "lower_diag"

# Fresh plotting copy
heatmap_plot <- heatmap_master %>%
  mutate(
    x_num = as.numeric(X_label),
    y_num = as.numeric(Y_label)
  )

if(mask_type == "upper"){
  heatmap_plot <- heatmap_plot %>%
    mutate(
      cor   = ifelse(x_num < y_num, NA, cor),
      label = ifelse(x_num < y_num, "", label)
    )
}

if(mask_type == "lower"){
  heatmap_plot <- heatmap_plot %>%
    mutate(
      cor   = ifelse(x_num > y_num, NA, cor),
      label = ifelse(x_num > y_num, "", label)
    )
}

if(mask_type == "upper_diag"){
  heatmap_plot <- heatmap_plot %>%
    mutate(
      cor   = ifelse(x_num <= y_num, NA, cor),
      label = ifelse(x_num <= y_num, "", label)
    )
}

if(mask_type == "lower_diag"){
  heatmap_plot <- heatmap_plot %>%
    mutate(
      cor   = ifelse(x_num >= y_num, NA, cor),
      label = ifelse(x_num >= y_num, "", label)
    )
}
 
## Remove values on the diagonal ONLY (self-correlations)
heatmap_plot <- heatmap_plot %>%
  mutate(
```

```{r}
# --- Palette prep (tone down viridis) ---
library(viridisLite)
library(colorspace)  # <-- use this for desaturate()
library(scales)      # for alpha() and squish

cols      <- viridisLite::viridis(256, begin = 0.2, end = 0.95)
soft_cols <- scales::alpha(colorspace::desaturate(cols, amount = 0.1), 0.85) # amount in desaturate() → higher = more muted (e.g., 0.5, 0.7) / alpha alpha(..., 0.85) → lower = lighter (e.g., 0.8).
# amount: 0 = no change; 1 = fully gray

# Plot

  geom_tile(linewidth = 0) + # Draws each heatmap tile (a square) with no border if linewidth = 0.
  geom_text(aes(label = label), # Adds text labels on tiles using the label column (e.g., 0.347*).
            size = 3.3, # cell text size (e.g., 0.347*)
            fontface = "bold", # use "plain" to "unbold"
            color = "black") +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = present) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = present) +  # Forces the axis order to match the vector (the list of condition names that actually exist in the data).

  #   limits = c(-0.2, 1),
  #   name = expression(italic(r)) # legend title
  # )
  
scale_fill_gradientn(
  colours = soft_cols, # reversed viridis color palette toned down (see above)
  limits  = c(0, 1), # or c(-0.2, 1) to show tiny negatives faintly
  oob     = scales::squish, # clip out-of-bounds to nearest limit

  y = NULL,

) +
coord_fixed() +
```

### HIPPOCAMPUS + RSC

 HC + RSC OL LATE MATRIX
```{r}

# --------------------------------
# 1) Filter + clean strings
# --------------------------------
heatmapFilter <- long_parsed %>%
  filter(
    ROI %in% c("RSC", "Hippocampus"),
    str_detect(raw_name, "ol_new_late_w_ol_new_late_")
  ) %>%
  group_by(ID, ROI, Hall) %>%
  mutate(
    # normalize the Hall names to avoid hidden mismatches
    Hall = str_squish(Hall),
    Hall = factor(Hall, levels = c("Cue period", "1st hallway", "2nd hallway", "Goal")),
    ROI  = str_squish(ROI)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Create combined condition label (normalized)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmapFilter <- heatmapFilter %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = str_squish(paste(ROI, Hall))
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Pivot to wide format
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_wide <- heatmapFilter %>%
  select(ID, Condition, RSA) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Condition,
    values_from = RSA
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Desired axis order (make sure it matches exactly)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
axis_order <- c(
  "Hippocampus Cue period",
  "Hippocampus 1st hallway",
  "Hippocampus 2nd hallway",
  "Hippocampus Goal",
  "RSC Cue period",
  "RSC 1st hallway",
  "RSC 2nd hallway",
  "RSC Goal"
)

# Sanity check
# print(setdiff(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide)))
# print(setdiff(colnames(heatmap_wide), axis_order))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute correlation matrix (restricted + reordered)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Keep only the columns in axis_order (in that order), dropping any others
present <- intersect(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide))
if (length(present) != length(axis_order)) {
  warning("Some expected conditions are missing: ",
          paste(setdiff(axis_order, present), collapse = ", "))
}
corr_matrix <- heatmap_wide %>%
  select(all_of(present)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Reorder rows/cols to the desired axis_order (for present labels)
corr_matrix <- corr_matrix[present, present, drop = FALSE]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute pairwise counts (n) and p-values for the matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------
data_wide <- heatmap_wide %>% select(all_of(present))
X <- as.matrix(data_wide)

# Pairwise non-NA counts: n_ij = number of rows where both cols i and j are not NA
ind   <- !is.na(X)
n_mat <- t(ind) %*% ind    # matrix of pairwise sample sizes

# We already have r_mat = corr_matrix (reordered to [present, present])
r_mat <- corr_matrix

# Compute p-values from r and n (two-sided); handle r = ±1, n < 3 safely
p_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(r_mat), ncol = ncol(r_mat),
                dimnames = dimnames(r_mat))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(r_mat))) {
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(r_mat))) {
    r <- r_mat[i, j]
    n <- n_mat[i, j]
    if (!is.na(r) && !is.na(n) && n >= 3) {
      if (abs(r) < 1) {
        tval <- r * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - r^2))
        pval <- 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = n - 2)
      } else {
        # Perfect correlation with >= 3 points -> p ~ 0
        pval <- 0
      }
      p_mat[i, j] <- pval
    } else {
      p_mat[i, j] <- NA_real_
    }
  }
}


# Choose which p-values to use for stars:
p_use <- p_mat  # or use p_adj_mat if you enabled BH correction above

# Build significance stars
stars_mat <- matrix("", nrow = nrow(p_use), ncol = ncol(p_use),
                    dimnames = dimnames(p_use))
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use < 0.001] <- "***"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.001 & p_use < 0.01] <- "**"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.01 & p_use < 0.05] <- "*"

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6)Convert correlation matrix (r mat) to long format and add p-values + stars
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(r_mat)) %>%
  rename(
    X_label = Var1,
    Y_label = Var2,
    cor     = Freq
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # attach p and stars from matrices (matching by dimnames)
    p_value = as.vector(p_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(p_mat)),
                                    match(Y_label, colnames(p_mat)))]),
    stars   = stars_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(stars_mat)),
                              match(Y_label, colnames(stars_mat)))],
    # format r with 3 decimals and append stars
    label_r = sprintf("%.3f", cor),
    label   = ifelse(is.na(cor), "", paste0(label_r, stars))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    X_label = factor(X_label, levels = present),
    Y_label = factor(Y_label, levels = present)
  )

# Freeze master copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df
# Freeze a clean copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df


```

```{r}
    # normalize the Hall names to avoid hidden mismatches
    Hall = str_squish(Hall),
    Hall = factor(Hall, levels = c("Cue period", "1st hallway", "2nd hallway", "Goal")),
    ROI  = str_squish(ROI)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Create combined condition label (normalized)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmapFilter <- heatmapFilter %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = str_squish(paste(ROI, Hall))
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Pivot to wide format
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_wide <- heatmapFilter %>%
  select(ID, Condition, RSA) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Condition,
    values_from = RSA
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Desired axis order (make sure it matches heatmap_wide df exactly)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
axis_order <- c(
  "Hippocampus Cue period",
  "Hippocampus 1st hallway",
  "Hippocampus 2nd hallway",
  "Hippocampus Goal",
  "Complex Cue period",
  "Complex 1st hallway",
  "Complex 2nd hallway",
  "Complex Goal"
)

# Sanity check
# print(setdiff(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide)))
# print(setdiff(colnames(heatmap_wide), axis_order))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute correlation matrix (restricted + reordered)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Keep only the columns in axis_order (in that order), dropping any others
present <- intersect(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide))
if (length(present) != length(axis_order)) {
  warning("Some expected conditions are missing: ",
          paste(setdiff(axis_order, present), collapse = ", "))
}
corr_matrix <- heatmap_wide %>%
  select(all_of(present)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Reorder rows/cols to the desired axis_order (for present labels)
corr_matrix <- corr_matrix[present, present, drop = FALSE]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute pairwise counts (n) and p-values for the matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------
data_wide <- heatmap_wide %>% select(all_of(present))
X <- as.matrix(data_wide)

# Pairwise non-NA counts: n_ij = number of rows where both cols i and j are not NA
ind   <- !is.na(X)
n_mat <- t(ind) %*% ind    # matrix of pairwise sample sizes

# We already have r_mat = corr_matrix (reordered to [present, present])
r_mat <- corr_matrix

# Compute p-values from r and n (two-sided); handle r = ±1, n < 3 safely
p_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(r_mat), ncol = ncol(r_mat),
                dimnames = dimnames(r_mat))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(r_mat))) {
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(r_mat))) {
    r <- r_mat[i, j]
    n <- n_mat[i, j]
    if (!is.na(r) && !is.na(n) && n >= 3) {
      if (abs(r) < 1) {
        tval <- r * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - r^2))
        pval <- 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = n - 2)
      } else {
        # Perfect correlation with >= 3 points -> p ~ 0
        pval <- 0
      }
      p_mat[i, j] <- pval
    } else {
      p_mat[i, j] <- NA_real_
    }
  }
}


# Choose which p-values to use for stars:
p_use <- p_mat  # or use p_adj_mat if you enabled BH correction above

# Build significance stars
stars_mat <- matrix("", nrow = nrow(p_use), ncol = ncol(p_use),
                    dimnames = dimnames(p_use))
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use < 0.001] <- "***"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.001 & p_use < 0.01] <- "**"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.01 & p_use < 0.05] <- "*"

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6)Convert correlation matrix (r mat) to long format and add p-values + stars
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(r_mat)) %>%
  rename(
    X_label = Var1,
    Y_label = Var2,
    cor     = Freq
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # attach p and stars from matrices (matching by dimnames)
    p_value = as.vector(p_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(p_mat)),
                                    match(Y_label, colnames(p_mat)))]),
    stars   = stars_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(stars_mat)),
                              match(Y_label, colnames(stars_mat)))],
    # format r with 3 decimals and append stars
    label_r = sprintf("%.3f", cor),
    label   = ifelse(is.na(cor), "", paste0(label_r, stars))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    X_label = factor(X_label, levels = present),
    Y_label = factor(Y_label, levels = present)
  )

# Freeze master copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df
# Freeze a clean copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df
```

```{r}
# --- Palette prep (tone down viridis) ---
library(viridisLite)
library(colorspace)  # <-- use this for desaturate()
library(scales)      # for alpha() and squish

cols      <- viridisLite::viridis(256, begin = 0.2, end = 0.95)
soft_cols <- scales::alpha(colorspace::desaturate(cols, amount = 0.1), 0.85) # amount in desaturate() → higher = more muted (e.g., 0.5, 0.7) / alpha alpha(..., 0.85) → lower = lighter (e.g., 0.8).
# amount: 0 = no change; 1 = fully gray

# Plot
ggplot(heatmap_plot, aes(x = X_label, y = Y_label, fill = cor)) +
  geom_tile(linewidth = 0) + # Draws each heatmap tile (a square) with no border if linewidth = 0.
  geom_text(aes(label = label), # Adds text labels on tiles using the label column (e.g., 0.347*).
            size = 3.3, # cell text size (e.g., 0.347*)
            fontface = "bold", # use "plain" to "unbold"
            color = "black") +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = present) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = present) +  # Forces the axis order to match the vector (the list of condition names that actually exist in the data).
  
  # scale_fill_gradient2( # Sets the color scale for fill
  #   low = "white", # for a 0-centered diverging scale with a few negative values, set a light color for negatives
  #   high = "blue",
  #   na.value = "white",
  #   midpoint = 0, # centers the color scale at 0 (useful for correlations)
  #   limits = c(-0.2, 1),
  #   name = expression(italic(r)) # legend title
  # )
  
scale_fill_gradientn(
  colours = soft_cols, # reversed viridis color palette toned down (see above)
  limits  = c(0, 1), # or c(-0.2, 1) to show tiny negatives faintly
  oob     = scales::squish, # clip out-of-bounds to nearest limit
  name    = expression(italic(r))
) + # virids is a continuous, color-blind friendly, color scale
  guides(
  fill = guide_colorbar(
    frame.colour   = "black",    # outline color of the colorbar
    frame.linewidth = 0.5,       # outline thickness
    ticks.colour   = "black"     # optional: tick marks on the bar
  )
) +
  
  scale_x_discrete(
  limits = present,
  labels = function(x) sub("^Complex", "RSComplex", x)  # rename df labels only for display
) +
scale_y_discrete(
  limits = present,
  labels = function(y) sub("^Complex", "RSComplex", y)  # rename df labels 
) +
  labs(
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  title = "HC + RSComplex OL LATE"
) +
coord_fixed() +
theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
theme(
  plot.title = element_text(
    hjust = 0.5,     # center title (0 = left, 1 = right)
    face = "bold",   # make title bold
    size = 12        # optional: adjust title size
  ),
  
  axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 45,
    hjust = 1,
    face = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ),
  axis.text.y = element_text(
    face = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ),
  panel.grid = element_blank(),
  legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(color = "black"),
  legend.key.height = unit(0.8, "cm"),
  legend.key.width  = unit(0.4, "cm")
)

ggsave("HC + RSComplex OL late_matrix.tiff",
```

```{r}
                                    match(Y_label, colnames(p_mat)))]),
    stars   = stars_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(stars_mat)),
                              match(Y_label, colnames(stars_mat)))],
    # format r with 3 decimals and append stars
    label_r = sprintf("%.3f", cor),
    label   = ifelse(is.na(cor), "", paste0(label_r, stars))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    X_label = factor(X_label, levels = present),
    Y_label = factor(Y_label, levels = present)
  )
```

## b) NON-OVERLAPPING MAZES FIRST

### HIPPOCAMPUS + RSC

 HC + RSC NOL EARLY

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# --------------------------------
# 1) Filter + clean strings
# --------------------------------
heatmapFilter <- long_parsed %>%
  filter(
    ROI %in% c("RSC", "Hippocampus"),
    str_detect(raw_name, "nol_new_early_w_nol_new_early_")
  ) %>%
  group_by(ID, ROI, Hall) %>%
  mutate(
    # normalize the Hall names to avoid hidden mismatches
    Hall = str_squish(Hall),
    Hall = factor(Hall, levels = c("Cue period", "1st hallway", "2nd hallway", "Goal")),
    ROI  = str_squish(ROI)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Create combined condition label (normalized)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmapFilter <- heatmapFilter %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = str_squish(paste(ROI, Hall))
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Pivot to wide format
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_wide <- heatmapFilter %>%
  select(ID, Condition, RSA) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Condition,
    values_from = RSA
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Desired axis order (make sure it matches exactly)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
axis_order <- c(
  "Hippocampus Cue period",
  "Hippocampus 1st hallway",
  "Hippocampus 2nd hallway",
  "Hippocampus Goal",
  "RSC Cue period",
  "RSC 1st hallway",
  "RSC 2nd hallway",
  "RSC Goal"
)

# Sanity check
# print(setdiff(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide)))
# print(setdiff(colnames(heatmap_wide), axis_order))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute correlation matrix (restricted + reordered)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Keep only the columns in axis_order (in that order), dropping any others
present <- intersect(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide))
if (length(present) != length(axis_order)) {
  warning("Some expected conditions are missing: ",
          paste(setdiff(axis_order, present), collapse = ", "))
}
corr_matrix <- heatmap_wide %>%
  select(all_of(present)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Reorder rows/cols to the desired axis_order (for present labels)
corr_matrix <- corr_matrix[present, present, drop = FALSE]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute pairwise counts (n) and p-values for the matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------
data_wide <- heatmap_wide %>% select(all_of(present))
X <- as.matrix(data_wide)

# Pairwise non-NA counts: n_ij = number of rows where both cols i and j are not NA
ind   <- !is.na(X)
n_mat <- t(ind) %*% ind    # matrix of pairwise sample sizes

# We already have r_mat = corr_matrix (reordered to [present, present])
r_mat <- corr_matrix

# Compute p-values from r and n (two-sided); handle r = ±1, n < 3 safely
p_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(r_mat), ncol = ncol(r_mat),
                dimnames = dimnames(r_mat))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(r_mat))) {
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(r_mat))) {
    r <- r_mat[i, j]
    n <- n_mat[i, j]
    if (!is.na(r) && !is.na(n) && n >= 3) {
      if (abs(r) < 1) {
        tval <- r * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - r^2))
        pval <- 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = n - 2)
      } else {
        # Perfect correlation with >= 3 points -> p ~ 0
        pval <- 0
      }
      p_mat[i, j] <- pval
    } else {
      p_mat[i, j] <- NA_real_
    }
  }
}


# Choose which p-values to use for stars:
p_use <- p_mat  # or use p_adj_mat if you enabled BH correction above

# Build significance stars
stars_mat <- matrix("", nrow = nrow(p_use), ncol = ncol(p_use),
                    dimnames = dimnames(p_use))
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use < 0.001] <- "***"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.001 & p_use < 0.01] <- "**"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.01 & p_use < 0.05] <- "*"

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6)Convert correlation matrix (r mat) to long format and add p-values + stars
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(r_mat)) %>%
  rename(
    X_label = Var1,
    Y_label = Var2,
    cor     = Freq
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # attach p and stars from matrices (matching by dimnames)
    p_value = as.vector(p_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(p_mat)),
                                    match(Y_label, colnames(p_mat)))]),
    stars   = stars_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(stars_mat)),
                              match(Y_label, colnames(stars_mat)))],
    # format r with 3 decimals and append stars
    label_r = sprintf("%.3f", cor),
    label   = ifelse(is.na(cor), "", paste0(label_r, stars))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    X_label = factor(X_label, levels = present),
    Y_label = factor(Y_label, levels = present)
  )

# Freeze master copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df
# Freeze a clean copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df


```

```{r}
            size = 3.3, # cell text size (e.g., 0.347*)
            fontface = "bold", # use "plain" to "unbold"
            color = "black") +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = present) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = present) +  # Forces the axis order to match the vector (the list of condition names that actually exist in the data).
  
  # scale_fill_gradient2( # Sets the color scale for fill
  #   low = "white", # for a 0-centered diverging scale with a few negative values, set a light color for negatives
  #   high = "blue",
  #   na.value = "white",
  #   midpoint = 0, # centers the color scale at 0 (useful for correlations)
  #   limits = c(-0.2, 1),
  #   name = expression(italic(r)) # legend title
  # )
  
scale_fill_gradientn(
  colours = soft_cols, # reversed viridis color palette toned down (see above)
  limits  = c(0, 1), # or c(-0.2, 1) to show tiny negatives faintly
  oob     = scales::squish, # clip out-of-bounds to nearest limit
  name    = expression(italic(r))
) + # virids is a continuous, color-blind friendly, color scale
  guides(
  fill = guide_colorbar(
    frame.colour   = "black",    # outline color of the colorbar
    frame.linewidth = 0.5,       # outline thickness
    ticks.colour   = "black"     # optional: tick marks on the bar
  )
) +
  labs(
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  title = "HC + RSC NOL LATE"
) +
coord_fixed() +
theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
theme(
  plot.title = element_text(
    hjust = 0.5,     # center title (0 = left, 1 = right)
    face = "bold",   # make title bold
    size = 12        # optional: adjust title size
  ),
  
  axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 45,
    hjust = 1,
    face = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ),
  axis.text.y = element_text(
    face = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ),
  panel.grid = element_blank(),
  legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(color = "black"),
  legend.key.height = unit(0.8, "cm"),
  legend.key.width  = unit(0.4, "cm")
)
```

### HIPPOCAMPUS + RSCOMPLEX

 HC + RSComplex NOL EARLY MATRIX

```{r}

# --------------------------------
# 1) Filter + clean strings
# --------------------------------
heatmapFilter <- long_parsed %>%
  filter(
    ROI %in% c("Complex", "Hippocampus"),
    str_detect(raw_name, "nol_new_early_w_nol_new_early_")
  ) %>%
  group_by(ID, ROI, Hall) %>%
  mutate(
    # normalize the Hall names to avoid hidden mismatches
    Hall = str_squish(Hall),
    Hall = factor(Hall, levels = c("Cue period", "1st hallway", "2nd hallway", "Goal")),
    ROI  = str_squish(ROI)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Create combined condition label (normalized)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmapFilter <- heatmapFilter %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = str_squish(paste(ROI, Hall))
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Pivot to wide format
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_wide <- heatmapFilter %>%
  select(ID, Condition, RSA) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Condition,
    values_from = RSA
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Desired axis order (make sure it matches exactly the heatmap_wide df labels)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
axis_order <- c(
  "Hippocampus Cue period",
  "Hippocampus 1st hallway",
  "Hippocampus 2nd hallway",
  "Hippocampus Goal",
  "Complex Cue period",
  "Complex 1st hallway",
  "Complex 2nd hallway",
  "Complex Goal"
)

# Sanity check
# print(setdiff(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide)))
# print(setdiff(colnames(heatmap_wide), axis_order))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute correlation matrix (restricted + reordered)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Keep only the columns in axis_order (in that order), dropping any others
present <- intersect(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide))
if (length(present) != length(axis_order)) {
  warning("Some expected conditions are missing: ",
          paste(setdiff(axis_order, present), collapse = ", "))
}
corr_matrix <- heatmap_wide %>%
  select(all_of(present)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Reorder rows/cols to the desired axis_order (for present labels)
corr_matrix <- corr_matrix[present, present, drop = FALSE]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute pairwise counts (n) and p-values for the matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------
data_wide <- heatmap_wide %>% select(all_of(present))
X <- as.matrix(data_wide)

# Pairwise non-NA counts: n_ij = number of rows where both cols i and j are not NA
ind   <- !is.na(X)
n_mat <- t(ind) %*% ind    # matrix of pairwise sample sizes

# We already have r_mat = corr_matrix (reordered to [present, present])
r_mat <- corr_matrix

# Compute p-values from r and n (two-sided); handle r = ±1, n < 3 safely
p_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(r_mat), ncol = ncol(r_mat),
                dimnames = dimnames(r_mat))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(r_mat))) {
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(r_mat))) {
    r <- r_mat[i, j]
    n <- n_mat[i, j]
    if (!is.na(r) && !is.na(n) && n >= 3) {
      if (abs(r) < 1) {
        tval <- r * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - r^2))
        pval <- 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = n - 2)
      } else {
        # Perfect correlation with >= 3 points -> p ~ 0
        pval <- 0
      }
      p_mat[i, j] <- pval
    } else {
      p_mat[i, j] <- NA_real_
    }
  }
}


# Choose which p-values to use for stars:
p_use <- p_mat  # or use p_adj_mat if you enabled BH correction above

# Build significance stars
stars_mat <- matrix("", nrow = nrow(p_use), ncol = ncol(p_use),
                    dimnames = dimnames(p_use))
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use < 0.001] <- "***"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.001 & p_use < 0.01] <- "**"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.01 & p_use < 0.05] <- "*"

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6)Convert correlation matrix (r mat) to long format and add p-values + stars
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(r_mat)) %>%
  rename(
    X_label = Var1,
    Y_label = Var2,
    cor     = Freq
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # attach p and stars from matrices (matching by dimnames)
    p_value = as.vector(p_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(p_mat)),
                                    match(Y_label, colnames(p_mat)))]),
    stars   = stars_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(stars_mat)),
                              match(Y_label, colnames(stars_mat)))],
    # format r with 3 decimals and append stars
    label_r = sprintf("%.3f", cor),
    label   = ifelse(is.na(cor), "", paste0(label_r, stars))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    X_label = factor(X_label, levels = present),
    Y_label = factor(Y_label, levels = present)
  )

# Freeze master copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df
# Freeze a clean copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df


```

```{r}
## MASKING (UPPER OR LOWER) TRIANGLES

# Choose masking type
mask_type <- "none"   # "none", "upper", "lower", "upper_diag", "lower_diag"

# Fresh plotting copy
heatmap_plot <- heatmap_master %>%
  mutate(
    x_num = as.numeric(X_label),
    y_num = as.numeric(Y_label)
  )

    )

    mutate(
      cor   = ifelse(x_num >= y_num, NA, cor),
      label = ifelse(x_num >= y_num, "", label)
    )
}
 
## Remove values on the diagonal ONLY (self-correlations)

  mutate(
    label = ifelse(X_label == Y_label, NA_character_, label)  # NA suppresses geom_text
  )
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
axis_order <- c(
  "RSC Cue period",
  "RSC 1st hallway",
  "RSC 2nd hallway",
  "RSC Goal",
  "Complex Cue period",
  "Complex 1st hallway",
  "Complex 2nd hallway",
  "Complex Goal"
)

# Sanity check
# print(setdiff(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide)))
# print(setdiff(colnames(heatmap_wide), axis_order))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute correlation matrix (restricted + reordered)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Keep only the columns in axis_order (in that order), dropping any others
present <- intersect(axis_order, colnames(heatmap_wide))
if (length(present) != length(axis_order)) {
  warning("Some expected conditions are missing: ",
          paste(setdiff(axis_order, present), collapse = ", "))
}
corr_matrix <- heatmap_wide %>%
  select(all_of(present)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Reorder rows/cols to the desired axis_order (for present labels)
corr_matrix <- corr_matrix[present, present, drop = FALSE]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Compute pairwise counts (n) and p-values for the matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------
data_wide <- heatmap_wide %>% select(all_of(present))
X <- as.matrix(data_wide)

# Pairwise non-NA counts: n_ij = number of rows where both cols i and j are not NA
ind   <- !is.na(X)
n_mat <- t(ind) %*% ind    # matrix of pairwise sample sizes

# We already have r_mat = corr_matrix (reordered to [present, present])
r_mat <- corr_matrix

# Compute p-values from r and n (two-sided); handle r = ±1, n < 3 safely
p_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(r_mat), ncol = ncol(r_mat),
                dimnames = dimnames(r_mat))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(r_mat))) {
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(r_mat))) {
    r <- r_mat[i, j]
    n <- n_mat[i, j]
    if (!is.na(r) && !is.na(n) && n >= 3) {
      if (abs(r) < 1) {
        tval <- r * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - r^2))
        pval <- 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = n - 2)
      } else {
        # Perfect correlation with >= 3 points -> p ~ 0
        pval <- 0
      }
      p_mat[i, j] <- pval
    } else {
      p_mat[i, j] <- NA_real_
    }
  }
}


# Choose which p-values to use for stars:
p_use <- p_mat  # or use p_adj_mat if you enabled BH correction above

# Build significance stars
stars_mat <- matrix("", nrow = nrow(p_use), ncol = ncol(p_use),
                    dimnames = dimnames(p_use))
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use < 0.001] <- "***"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.001 & p_use < 0.01] <- "**"
stars_mat[!is.na(p_use) & p_use >= 0.01 & p_use < 0.05] <- "*"

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6)Convert correlation matrix (r mat) to long format and add p-values + stars
# ------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(r_mat)) %>%
  rename(
    X_label = Var1,
    Y_label = Var2,
    cor     = Freq
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # attach p and stars from matrices (matching by dimnames)
    p_value = as.vector(p_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(p_mat)),
                                    match(Y_label, colnames(p_mat)))]),
    stars   = stars_mat[cbind(match(X_label, rownames(stars_mat)),
                              match(Y_label, colnames(stars_mat)))],
    # format r with 3 decimals and append stars
    label_r = sprintf("%.3f", cor),
    label   = ifelse(is.na(cor), "", paste0(label_r, stars))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    X_label = factor(X_label, levels = present),
    Y_label = factor(Y_label, levels = present)
  )

# Freeze master copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df
# Freeze a clean copy
heatmap_master <- heatmap_df
```

```{r}
# --- Palette prep (tone down viridis) ---
library(viridisLite)
library(colorspace)  # <-- use this for desaturate()
library(scales)      # for alpha() and squish

cols      <- viridisLite::viridis(256, begin = 0.2, end = 0.95)
soft_cols <- scales::alpha(colorspace::desaturate(cols, amount = 0.1), 0.85) # amount in desaturate() → higher = more muted (e.g., 0.5, 0.7) / alpha alpha(..., 0.85) → lower = lighter (e.g., 0.8).
# amount: 0 = no change; 1 = fully gray

# Plot
ggplot(heatmap_plot, aes(x = X_label, y = Y_label, fill = cor)) +
  geom_tile(linewidth = 0) + # Draws each heatmap tile (a square) with no border if linewidth = 0.
  geom_text(aes(label = label), # Adds text labels on tiles using the label column (e.g., 0.347*).
            size = 3.3, # cell text size (e.g., 0.347*)
            fontface = "bold", # use "plain" to "unbold"
            color = "black") +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = present) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = present) +  # Forces the axis order to match the vector (the list of condition names that actually exist in the data).
  
  # scale_fill_gradient2( # Sets the color scale for fill
  #   low = "white", # for a 0-centered diverging scale with a few negative values, set a light color for negatives
  #   high = "blue",
  #   na.value = "white",
  #   midpoint = 0, # centers the color scale at 0 (useful for correlations)
  #   limits = c(-0.2, 1),
  #   name = expression(italic(r)) # legend title
  # )
  
scale_fill_gradientn(
  colours = soft_cols, # reversed viridis color palette toned down (see above)
  limits  = c(0, 1), # or c(-0.2, 1) to show tiny negatives faintly
  oob     = scales::squish, # clip out-of-bounds to nearest limit
  name    = expression(italic(r))
) + # virids is a continuous, color-blind friendly, color scale
  guides(
  fill = guide_colorbar(
    frame.colour   = "black",    # outline color of the colorbar
    frame.linewidth = 0.5,       # outline thickness
    ticks.colour   = "black"     # optional: tick marks on the bar
  )
) +
  scale_x_discrete(
  limits = present,
  labels = function(x) sub("^Complex", "RSComplex", x)  # rename df labels only for display
) +
scale_y_discrete(
  limits = present,
  labels = function(y) sub("^Complex", "RSComplex", y)  # rename df labels 
) +
  
  labs(
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  title = "RSC + RSComplex NOL EARLY"
) +
coord_fixed() +
theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
theme(
  plot.title = element_text(
    hjust = 0.5,     # center title (0 = left, 1 = right)
    face = "bold",   # make title bold
    size = 12        # optional: adjust title size
  ),
  
  axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 45,
    hjust = 1,
    face = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ),
  axis.text.y = element_text(
    face = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ),
  panel.grid = element_blank(),
  legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(color = "black"),
  legend.key.height = unit(0.8, "cm"),
  legend.key.width  = unit(0.4, "cm")
)
```
